analysis: R-Drop trial succeeded with host validation macro HR@10=0.5650, improving by 0.0388 over the preceding 0.5262 result but remaining 0.0087 below the reported best 0.5737. Per-category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.595, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.600, Electronics 0.430, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.635. Electronics remains the weakest category. Dropout consistency is promising relative to the preceding objective, but this trial does not establish a causal explanation or a new best result. Allocated GPU time was 442.67 seconds; no test metrics were available.
code_summary: Trains one independent GRURec model per category: 96-dimensional item embeddings, two-layer GRU, causal attention over earlier recurrent states with learned relative-distance bias, projected recurrent/attention features, and a jointly trained gated item-identity residual. Scores use normalized item similarity with learned scale and item bias. Training reuses one positive and 64 sampled negatives across two shared-parameter dropout passes, averages their BPR-max losses, and adds 0.1 times symmetric KL consistency computed in float32 at valid positions. Prediction uses one deterministic forward pass from exactly one selected checkpoint per category, with no ensemble or checkpoint averaging. Preserves dataset routing, trial-local artifacts, seed 42, and the 200-epoch environment default.
